title: Sidelens minimap: condensed telemetry & rollout controls for console navigation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Surface a compact, persistent 'Sidelens' minimap in the console that gives engineers and product owners glanceable telemetry (per-route latency/cost/err rates), quick rollout controls (canary/rollback), and workspace switching without taking full canvas space. The minimap should allow people to: 1) see health and cost hotspots across routes and models, 2) expand to a route inspector for quick config changes (traffic split, fallback policies), and 3) switch workspaces or jump to a full dashboard. This ticket drives the high-fidelity prototype, interaction specs, and developer handoff for the smallest-viable Sidelens (collapsed/peek/expanded states).

Constraints & non-goals: We must keep the Sidelens width <= 360px when expanded to avoid occluding the main editor/workspace; it should be keyboard-accessible; not intended to replace full dashboards (links out to console dashboards remain). Backend telemetry endpoints will be mocked for the prototype; final integration handled in a separate ENG ticket.

Deliverables: Figma prototype (collapsed, peek, expanded), interaction spec (keyboard + mouse + touch), accessibility checklist (contrast, focus order), microcopy for rollout actions, and an A/B test plan for measuring impact on rollout MTTR and dashboard navigation time.

Design decisions summary: - Use a 3-band visual treatment for route tiles (green/yellow/red) with inline sparkline for latency. - Compress workspace chips into an overflow popover to enable fast switching without a dedicated dropdown. - Rollout controls are inline micro-actions (Canary 10% / Promote / Rollback) with confirmation modal for destructive actions. - Cost lens uses 24h rolling cost and 30d trend (icon and delta), with a lightweight tooltip to avoid heavy queries on hover.

Trade-offs considered: - Inline telemetry vs. click-to-fetch: chose inline summarised metrics to minimise clicks, but full metrics require opening the route inspector (to avoid frequent expensive API calls). - Persistent minimap position: fixed right-side vs left-side. We recommend right-side for parity with common observability UIs and to preserve left rail for core navigation.

Acceptance criteria: - Figma prototype demonstrates the three states with accessible keyboard flows documented. - Usability test with 6 internal participants shows >80% success on 'switch workspace' and 'promote canary' tasks and median time under 25s. - Handoff ZIP includes annotated components, CSS tokens, and interaction notes for ENG.
comments: 2026-03-01 Maya Chen: Initial research synthesis added — highlighted that platform engineers want rollouts adjacent to latency views to reduce context switching.
2026-03-03 Lucas Ortega: First-pass wireframes uploaded to Figma (link in attachments). Asking ENG for mocked telemetry endpoints and a lightweight feature flag to toggle Sidelens in staging.
2026-03-05 PM review (Aisha Patel): Requested clearer error-states for partial telemetry and suggested adding a 'last-updated' timestamp to avoid stale impressions.

2026-03-07 Accessibility review (Jon R.) : Focus order needs adjustment — 'Promote' should be reachable via Enter from the collapsed focus state. Also flagged color contrast for the 3-band treatment on small chips.

2026-03-09 Prototype usability session: 6 participants (2 platform eng, 2 PMs, 2 SREs). Findings: workspace switching flow intuitive (5/6 success), cost delta misunderstood by one participant — updated microcopy to '24h cost change'.
2026-03-10 Handoff: Prepared interaction spec and component token table. Punted full telemetry integration to ENG-19754. Marked ready for dev review and design QA.
2026-03-10 Lucas Ortega: Added proposed rollout microcopy and error recovery flow (cancel & resume). Will follow up with engineering on API contract next week.
